meta.region: United Kingdom (focus: England; notes for Wales and Scotland)
meta.purpose: Reference data for Insulation Planner (UK): targets, U-value conventions, products, retail prices and installed costs.
meta.conventions: Every numeric entry carries a source id (see sources[]) and confidence. Unverified values are null with a note. "derived" means arithmetic on cited inputs.
caveats: Web search budget was exhausted mid-research; some items (blown-loft installed cost per m2, cellulose/sheep wool/vermiculite lambda, XPS manufacturer lambda, ISO 6946 Table 9 intermediate roof-space value) remain null.
B&Q prices unavailable (site returned 503 to automated access); Screwfix stocked no mineral-wool rolls or PIR boards online.
Retail prices are a single-day snapshot (2026-10-14) and include promotions (Wickes Knauf Space rolls all GBP 27 on offer).
ADL 2026 (Future Homes Standard) takes effect 24 Mar 2027 and does not change existing-dwelling U-value targets.

england.note: Approved Document L Volume 1 (2021 edition incorporating 2023 amendments) is current guidance in England. The 2026 edition was published 24 Mar 2026 (revised 8 Sep 2026) and takes effect 24 Mar 2027 (24 Sep 2027 for higher-risk building work); its existing-dwelling tables (renumbered 3.2 and 3.3) carry the same values as 2021 Tables 4.2 and 4.3.

retainedOrRenovatedElements_ADL2021_Tabl.description: Limiting U-values for existing elements in existing dwellings. Column (a) threshold: retained elements worse than this should be upgraded. Column (b) improved: target U-value for renovated or upgraded elements.

rows.element: Pitched roof - insulation at ceiling level (loft)
rows.note: ADL 2021 Table 4.3 has a single "Roof" row covering all roof types (pitched at ceiling, pitched at rafters, flat); the same 0.35/0.16 applies to each.

rows.element: Pitched roof - insulation at rafter level (room in roof / warm loft)
rows.note: Single "Roof" row. Note 3: if meeting the standard would limit head room, a lesser standard may be appropriate, provided insulation plus any air gap is at least the rafter depth and the lowest practicable U-value insulant is used.

rows.element: Flat roof or roof with integral insulation
rows.note: Single "Roof" row. Note 4: lesser standard may be appropriate where load-bearing capacity of frame or upstand height is a problem.
Note 5: applies only to a wall suitable for cavity insulation; otherwise treat as internal/external insulation.

rows.element: Wall - internal or external insulation (solid wall, IWI/EWI)
rows.note: Note 6: if meeting the standard would reduce the room floor area by more than 5%, a lesser standard may be appropriate.
Note 8: lesser standard may be appropriate where adjoining floor levels would be significantly affected.

rules.rule: Renovation of >50% of an individual thermal element, or a major renovation (>25% of the envelope surface area), triggers upgrading the whole element to column (b).
If column (b) is not technically/functionally feasible or would not achieve a simple payback of 15 years or less, upgrade to the lowest U-value that is feasible within a 15-year payback.
Generally an upgraded thermal element should not have a U-value greater than 0.7 W/m2K (lesser standard acceptable if Part C condensation requirements are met).
Renovation includes: new cladding/render layer, dry-lining, stripping to structure and rebuilding, replacing a flat roof membrane, and providing cavity wall insulation.

appendixC_typicalConstructions.works: Renewal of roof covering / ceiling, cold loft (no living accommodation), existing loft insulation <50mm or poor
appendixC_typicalConstructions.typicalConstruction: 250mm mineral fibre or cellulose fibre quilt between and across ceiling joists, or loose fill or equivalent

appendixC_typicalConstructions.works: Renewal of roof covering, existing loft insulation 50-100mm in good condition
appendixC_typicalConstructions.typicalConstruction: Top up loft insulation to at least 250mm mineral fibre or cellulose fibre (may be boarded out)

appendixC_typicalConstructions.works: Flat roof renewal of covering, existing insulation <100mm mineral fibre or poor
Solid wall: dry-lining or EWI when renewing finishes
appendixC_typicalConstructions.note: Accept up to 5% loss of room area; where insulation is returned at party walls the target may rise to 0.35 or above.

appendixC_typicalConstructions.works: Ground floor renovation (screed or timber deck replacement)
appendixC_typicalConstructions.note: Added insulation likely cost-effective where existing floor U > 0.70.

newElementsInExistingDwellings_ADL2021_T.description: Limiting U-values for new (or replacement) fabric elements in existing dwellings, e.g. extensions. Area-weighted except windows/doors/rooflights.

rows.note: Lesser provision may be appropriate if meeting it would reduce room floor area by >5%.
Lesser provision may be appropriate where adjoining floor levels are a problem; extension floor may use whole-dwelling perimeter/area.

rows.alternative: Window Energy Rating Band B minimum
Doorset Energy Rating Band C minimum
Doorset Energy Rating Band B minimum

futureHomesStandard_ADL2026.renamedTo: Approved Document L: Energy and greenhouse gas emissions (2026 edition)
futureHomesStandard_ADL2026.existingDwellingChanges: No change to limiting U-values for existing dwellings: 2026 Table 3.2 (new elements in existing dwellings: roof 0.15, wall 0.18, floor 0.18, windows 1.4/WER B) and Table 3.3 (retained/renovated: roof 0.35->0.16, cavity 0.70->0.55, IWI/EWI 0.70->0.30, floor 0.70->0.25) match 2021 Tables 4.2/4.3. The 15-year simple payback test, the 0.7 W/m2K cap and Appendix C (250mm mineral fibre loft) are retained. The 2021 timber window/door transitional notes are removed. Main 2026 changes (new-build notional dwelling, heat, Requirement L3 renewable electricity) do not alter retrofit insulation targets.

loftDepthMm.text: Current building regulations recommend a minimum depth of 270mm for mineral wool insulation.

loftTopUpExample.note: EST notes 270mm is "the minimum recommendation for new builds". Savings basis not stated on page.

loftMethod.text: First layer of mineral wool rolls between joists, second layer at right angles across joists to reach depth; do not squash mineral wool (reduces effectiveness); leave a ventilation gap below boards; do not cover vents.

floors.note: EST states floors should achieve 0.25 (E/W/NI) or 0.18 (Scotland) and that at least 70mm high-performance rigid foam or around 150mm mineral wool is typically needed. The Scotland figure conflicts with the April 2026 Scottish handbook Table 6.2 floor value of 0.15 (applies to alterations/extensions) - treat Scotland value as uncertain.

walls.note: Cavity wall insulation needs a cavity at least 50mm wide, clear of rubble; narrow cavities (<50mm, often pre-1920s) are a risk. A brick wall 260-350mm thick is likely a cavity wall; thinner is probably solid. Guarantee: 25 years via CIGA or insurance-backed.

solidWallWarning.text: Oct 2025 National Audit Office report on quality failures in EWI/IWI under government schemes; EST reports 98% of homes fitted with EWI under ECO4/GBIS have problems needing fixing (TrustMark Find & Fix audits).

wales.note: Wales has its own Approved Document L. 2022 edition current; 2026 edition takes effect 4 Mar 2027 with the same fabric values. In Wales, retained/renovated elements should be upgraded to column (a); column (b) is the worst acceptable when (a) is not feasible.

retained_Table11_1.note: Partially filled cavities exempt from column (a); exposed sites may be exempt from CWI.

newElementsInExistingDwellings_Table4_1.note: Stricter than England for roofs (0.13 vs 0.15) and floors (0.15 vs 0.18).

scotland.note: Scotland uses Building Standards Technical Handbooks (Section 6 Energy), not Approved Documents. April 2026 edition applies to warrant applications on/after 6 Apr 2026.

table6_2_maxU_newAndAlterations.note: Applies to new buildings and to alteration, extension or conversion of existing buildings (clause 6.2.1). Individual localised elements no worse than 0.7 (walls/floors) or 0.35 (roofs).

alterations.text: Where an envelope element is altered/rebuilt, Table 6.2 values are benchmarks to be met as far as reasonably practicable; in most cases a roof should achieve at least 0.35 and a wall or floor 0.70 average. Infill of small openings (about 4 m2 or less) should match the surrounding element but be no worse than 0.70 (wall/floor) or 0.35 (roof).

loftDepthClaim.text: Knauf states building regulations require a minimum loft depth of 270mm (350mm in Scotland).
loftDepthClaim.note: Manufacturer statement; not found as a prescribed depth in the Scottish handbook (which sets U-values).

method.text: ADL requires U-values assessed using BR 443 conventions; BR 443 uses BS EN ISO 6946 (above-ground elements, combined upper/lower-limit method for bridged layers) and BS EN ISO 13370 (ground floors, depends on perimeter/area ratio). Simple formula for unbridged build-ups: U = 1 / (Rsi + sum(d/lambda) + Rse). Use nominal thickness except where compressible insulation is constrained (use installed thickness). Use manufacturer declared lambda where available.

surfaceResistances_ISO6946.heatFlow: horizontal (walls, windows; within +/-30 deg of horizontal)

surfaceResistances_ISO6946.note: Roof pitches of 60 deg or less are treated as upward heat flow.
For ground floors Rse is not used; ISO 13370 handles the ground.

layerResistances.inputs: br443 lambda 0.21 W/mK (standard wallboard up to 700 kg/m3)
br443 default brick lambda outer leaf 0.77
br443 default brick lambda inner leaf 0.56

layerResistances.layer: Unventilated airspace >=25mm with low-emissivity (foil) surface, e=0.2
Plasterboard on dabs: 15mm airspace (dabs 20% of area, dab lambda 0.43)
Roof void between rafters and flat ceiling (rafter-level insulation, flat ceiling)
Ventilated loft/roof space above insulated ceiling (BS EN ISO 6946 Table 9, includes roof covering; excludes Rse=0.04)
layerResistances.note: BR 443 gives the range 0.06 (tiled roof, no felt/boards) to 0.3 (roof lined with boards and felt). The intermediate ISO 6946 Table 9 category (felt OR boards under tiles - the common UK case) was not verified in an accessible source; null. Knauf typical loft U-values assume "cold ventilated roof with felt or sarking boards".

layerResistances.layer: Ventilated cladding cavity behind tile-hanging etc. (use as Rse, ignore layers outside)

materialConductivities.note: Manufacturer U-value table assumption; BR 443 says use manufacturer/CIBSE Guide A/BS EN 1745 data.
Knauf existing-cavity tables also use unnamed block values of 0.51 and 0.34 W/mK.

timberFractions_BR443.inputs: br443 formula width/spacing + 0.01; Knauf loft tables quote 8.8% per BR443

timberFractions_BR443.case: Suspended timber ground floor joists, default (38mm at 400mm + nogging every 3m)

timberFractions_BR443.note: 0.125 allowed if single top plate, sole plate below FFL, no mid-height noggings, junction studs <=38mm deep with insulation behind.

timberFractions_BR443.case: Rafters - no BR 443 default; use width/spacing + 0.01
timberFractions_BR443.inputs: br443 general rule (examples in BR 443: 35@600 = 0.068, 50@400 = 0.135). Knauf solutions guide assumes 38mm rafters at 600mm = 6.3% (no +1%).

timberFractions_BR443.case: Dry-lining battens 47mm at 600mm incl. top/bottom rails (2.4m room)

corrections.item: Air gaps in insulation, level 0 (no gaps; e.g. second layer covering joists)
Air gaps level 1 (default; e.g. insulation between joists/rafters only)
Air gaps level 2 (air circulation possible, e.g. loose partial-fill boards)
corrections.note: Air-gap corrections apply to walls and roofs, not floors.
Typical +9% at U=0.16. Table extracted from PDF with imperfect layout: 0mm -> 0.015, 25mm -> 0.006, 50mm -> 0.003 (hatch insulation lambda 0.040).

loftLayering.text: Pitched roof at ceiling level: U-value calculated at the ceiling plane; joists + insulation between them is a bridged layer; a second cross-laid layer is continuous. Knauf: 100mm between joists + 170mm over joists (270mm, LR44) gives U=0.16; 100mm + 150mm (250mm, LR40) gives 0.16 (100x47 joists at 400mm, 12.8% timber, 12.5mm plasterboard, ventilated roof with felt or sarking boards).

rollQuantity.formula: rolls per layer = loft length (m) x loft width (m) / area per roll (m2); for the base layer add about 0.3m per run where it meets the eaves
rollQuantity.note: Rolls are sold by area per pack; first layer is cut to joist spacing (combi-cut perforated at 2x600/3x400mm or 2x570/3x380mm).

cavityFillTypicalU_existingWalls.product: Knauf Supafil 40 blown into existing brick/cavity/100mm inner leaf, plasterboard on dabs
cavityFillTypicalU_existingWalls.note: Range across inner leaf brick 0.56, block 1.13, 0.51, 0.34 W/mK.

floors.text: Ground-floor U-values depend on perimeter/area ratio (BS EN ISO 13370); exposed perimeter excludes party walls. Uninsulated large floors can already be 0.15-0.35 depending on size (BR 443 Appendix B). For a simplified calculator, take insulation R and apply ISO 13370 or use manufacturer P/A tables.

oldMineralWool.note: RdSAP Table 14 uses lambda 0.04 W/mK as typical for mineral wool, rock wool, fibre glass or EPS. Current commodity glass wool loft roll is 0.044 (Knauf/Isover). Old insulation that is compressed, damp, displaced or settled will perform worse than its nominal thickness (EST: squashing mineral wool reduces effectiveness).
oldMineralWool.rValueInputs: R = thickness / lambda using rdsap10 lambda 0.04 and current commodity loft-roll lambda 0.044 (knauf-lr44-readycut)
oldMineralWool.rValueNote: For lofts, prefer the RdSAP Table 16 U-values below (they already include joists and the roof space). RdSAP Table 14 (used for walls) tabulates R = 0.025 x T + 0.25 at lambda 0.04, i.e. it adds 0.25 m2K/W to d/lambda; do not use those figures as pure insulation R.

rdsapLoftUValuesByThickness.description: Assumed roof U-value at ceiling level for an existing loft, by measured insulation thickness (mineral wool or EPS; includes joists and roof-space sheltering). Useful to estimate the starting U-value.
rdsapLoftUValuesByThickness.note: Insulation taken as between joists up to 150mm and between+over joists above that. If retrofit insulation of unknown thickness is present, RdSAP uses 50mm.

rows.wall: Solid brick as built, 200-280mm thick (bands A-E)

vermiculite.note: No verified lambda found. RdSAP Table 16 applies to mineral wool/EPS only; for other loft materials it falls back to age-band defaults (Table 18), so a calculator should treat vermiculite as "unknown/do not count" rather than estimate its R-value.

asbestosWarning.text: Loose vermiculite loft insulation (grey-brown/gold granules) may be contaminated with asbestos. Assume it contains asbestos and do not disturb, remove or lay new insulation over it yourself; get it tested/handled by a licensed asbestos professional. Separately, loose-fill asbestos insulation (fluffy blue-grey or whitish) can be found in loft spaces, cavities and under floors and is among the most dangerous asbestos materials.
asbestosWarning.context: US EPA: Libby (Montana) mine supplied >70% of US vermiculite 1919-1990 (sold as Zonolite) and was contaminated with asbestos; EPA advises assuming any vermiculite insulation contains asbestos. EPA is a US source - no UK-specific vermiculite guidance was located; HSE covers loose-fill asbestos in loft spaces.
